summary.title: Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training

setting_and_object.category: Architecture (test-time-training MLLM for streaming spatial understanding)

details: Spatial intelligence requires progressively accumulating 3D evidence from unbounded video streams, but MLLMs are limited to short clips (16-32 frames): naively extending context is quadratically expensive and subsampling discards fine spatial detail.
Existing spatial-QA supervision is sparse and local (short answers about two objects), giving weak signal for learning how to maintain a persistent global spatial memory.

Spatial-TTT: an MLLM whose decoder interleaves test-time-training layers (fast weights updated online by gradient steps on a self-supervised key-value prediction loss, acting as compact non-linear memory) with self-attention 'anchor' layers, so long streams are compressed into fast weights while pretrained full-context reasoning is preserved.

Spatial-predictive mechanism: replaces point-wise linear Q/K/V for the TTT branch with lightweight depth-wise 3D spatiotemporal convolutions over the token grid, so fast weights learn predictive mappings between spatiotemporal contexts (geometric correspondence, temporal continuity) rather than isolated tokens.

Practical scalability: large-chunk fast-weight updates (LaCT-style) run in parallel with sliding-window attention whose window covers the chunk, restoring intra-chunk causal interaction; plus a dense 3D scene-description dataset that supervises the fast-weight update dynamics.
Initialized from Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct; TTT layers replace 3 of every 4 attention layers (75% TTT, 25% anchor).
TTT layers reuse the pretrained QKV projections plus learnable scale/shift on q,k; gating projection zero-initialized; fast-weight network is a bias-free SwiGLU MLP.

Depthwise 3D convolutions with 3x3x3 kernels, Dirac-initialized so the model initially matches the original full-attention model; Muon update rule (momentum + Newton-Schulz orthogonalization) with L2-norm weight renormalization.

Chunk size b=2648; sliding window w initialized at 5600 and annealed to 2648; inference uses dual KV cache (fixed-length SWA cache + pending cache flushed at chunk size) for constant-memory streaming.

Stage 1: ~16K dense scene-description samples built from SceneVerse 3D scene graphs (3.6K ScanNet, 12.5K ARKitScenes), targets are scene walkthroughs covering scene type, object categories/counts, and pairwise spatial relations; 32 frames sampled; window annealing over first two epochs.

Stage 2: ~3M spatial VQA (≈2.5M open-source: VSI-590K, VLM-3R, InternSpatial, ViCA; ≈0.5M self-built from ScanNet/ScanNet++ with room extents, OBBs, 2D semantic projections), 64-128 frames, w=b fixed.
Learning rates 1e-6 (backbone) / 1e-5 (new TTT parameters), 1k warmup steps, cosine schedule.
VSI-Bench (>5,000 QA over 288 indoor videos; ACC for MC, MRA for numerical, macro average).
MindCube-Tiny (1,050 multi-view questions: Among/Around/Rotation), accuracy.
VSI-SUPER-Recall (ACC) and VSI-SUPER-Count (MRA) for long-horizon streaming spatial sensing across increasing video lengths.
Proprietary: GPT-5, Gemini-3-Pro, Seed-2.0, Kimi-K2.5.
Open general MLLMs: Qwen3-VL and Qwen2.5-VL series, InternVL3, LLaVA-OneVision/Video.
Spatial models: VST, Cambrian-S, Spatial-MLLM, MindCube-3B; long-video baselines MovieChat and Flash-VStream for VSI-SUPER; human and random references.
Variants: w/o spatial-predictive mechanism (identity in place of 3D conv), w/o dense scene-description data, w/o hybrid architecture (no self-attention anchor layers).
Decoding memory and theoretical TFLOPs measured versus input frame count (up to 1024 frames) against Qwen3-VL-2B and Spatial-MLLM.

key_findings.finding: A 2B model with online fast-weight memory achieves state-of-the-art general video spatial understanding, beating much larger proprietary and open models.
key_findings.evidence: Spatial-TTT-2B reaches 64.4 average on VSI-Bench (best on Relative Direction, Route Plan, Absolute Distance, and competitive on Room Size/Object Count) and 76.2 accuracy on MindCube-Tiny, +12.3 points over Gemini-3-Pro (63.9) and +24.5 over MindCube-3B (51.7).

key_findings.finding: Streaming fast-weight updates keep spatial performance stable as video length grows, whereas context-bound baselines collapse.
key_findings.evidence: On VSI-SUPER, Spatial-TTT is competitive on Recall across durations and significantly outperforms all baselines on Count; general/spatial MLLMs (Qwen3-VL, Cambrian-S) degrade sharply on longer videos due to context-budget/OOM limits, and long-video models (MovieChat, Flash-VStream) underperform at all durations.

key_findings.finding: The hybrid interleaving of TTT with self-attention anchor layers is the single most critical design choice.
key_findings.evidence: Removing anchor layers drops VSI-Bench average from 64.4 to 53.9, with multiple-choice falling from 64.8 to 52.4.

key_findings.finding: Both the spatial-predictive convolutional Q/K/V and dense scene-description supervision contribute substantially, mainly to metric/numerical spatial reasoning and long-horizon memory.
key_findings.evidence: Removing the SP-mechanism lowers average to 62.1 (numerical 64.0 to 60.7, with notable Route Plan decline); removing dense data lowers average to 61.3 (numerical -3.0, multiple-choice -3.3, with marked drops on Room Size, Relative Direction, Appearance Order).

key_findings.finding: The architecture attains near-linear compute/memory scaling with frame count, unlike quadratic-attention or geometry-encoder baselines.
key_findings.evidence: Doubling input length roughly doubles compute; at 1024 frames Spatial-TTT cuts both TFLOPs and memory by over 40% versus Qwen3-VL-2B, while Spatial-MLLM scales super-linearly and OOMs beyond 256 frames.
